summary: This wiki note traces Eric Clapton's career after his alcoholism treatment at Hazelden, covering his recovery-era albums, collaborations with Roger Waters and Phil Collins, and his charity performances. It also covers his 2005 Cream reunion concerts and the release of the album Back Home. The content is drawn from a Wikipedia-style biography excerpt.
one_line: Eric Clapton's post-rehab career in the 1980s and 2000s, including albums, charity concerts, Live Aid, and the Cream reunion.
key_facts: After being discharged, doctors at Hazelden recommended that Eric Clapton not partake in any activities that would act as triggers for his alcoholism or stress.
A few months after his discharge, Eric Clapton began working on his next album, against doctors' orders.
Working with Tom Dowd, Eric Clapton produced what he thought was his "most forced" album to date, Money and Cigarettes.
Clapton chose the album name Money and Cigarettes "because that's all I saw myself having left" after his first rehabilitation from alcoholism.
In 1984 Clapton performed on Roger Waters' solo album The Pros and Cons of Hitch Hiking and joined the supporting tour.
In 2006 Clapton and Roger Waters performed at Highclere Castle in aid of the Countryside Alliance, playing "Wish You Were Here" and "Comfortably Numb".
Clapton played at the Live Aid concert at John F. Kennedy Stadium in Philadelphia on 13 July 1985, playing with Phil Collins, among others.
Clapton's 1985 album Behind the Sun, produced with Phil Collins, produced the hits "Forever Man" and "She's Waiting".
Clapton's 1986 album August was another album produced with Phil Collins.
On 22 January 2005, Clapton performed in the Tsunami Relief Concert at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff, in aid of victims of the 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake.
In May 2005, Clapton, Jack Bruce, and Ginger Baker reunited as Cream for a series of concerts at the Royal Albert Hall in London.
Cream later performed in New York at Madison Square Garden.
Clapton's album Back Home was his first album of new original material in nearly five years and was released on Reprise Records on 30 August.
